findings.detail: Lightning Arrow is level 15 in a 4-link with Mirage Archer, Added Lightning Damage, and Elemental Damage with Attacks. It has no projectile-spread support in this export, so damage can be reasonable while packs still feel under-covered.
findings.action: Try LMP or GMP in place of Added Lightning Damage for clear. This trades damage per projectile for wider coverage; keep the current link for tougher targets if it performs better.

findings.title: The bow is the clearest sustained-damage upgrade
findings.detail: Rage Wing is an item-level 42 Decurve Bow on a level 60 character. It has useful flat Fire and Lightning damage and 10% crafted attack speed, but is now 18 character levels behind. The current quiver is a good flat-elemental upgrade.
findings.action: Prioritize a faster bow with strong added elemental attack damage. A 5-link is the next dependable link upgrade after the weapon.

findings.title: Life is the main defensive gap
findings.detail: PoB reports 2,186 Life with capped Fire/Cold/Lightning resistance at 75/76/75 after the configured -30 resistance penalty, +7% Chaos Resistance, 100% effective Spell Suppression, and 6,291 Armour. Helm, gloves, and boots contribute little Life.
findings.action: Add Life on weak gear slots while preserving resistance caps. A reasonable next checkpoint is over about 2,500 Life before maps.

findings.title: The Warden shock setup is online; burst ascendancy is still ahead
findings.detail: Oath of Spring is allocated, and Storm Rain is linked to Overcharge, Unbound Ailments, and Greater Multiple Projectiles. Avatar of the Wilds is not allocated in this snapshot. In 3.29, it grants 100% more Elemental Damage while Unbound for 10 seconds after reaching 100 Unbound Fury.
findings.action: Use Storm Rain and Sniper’s Mark on tougher rares and bosses. Take Avatar of the Wilds with the next Labyrinth when it is safe; it improves burst damage, not Lightning Arrow coverage.

findings.title: Precise Technique is not confirmed by this export
findings.detail: This export reports 1,514 Main Hand Accuracy versus 2,186 maximum Life and 7.1% critical chance. Those calculations do not corroborate Precise Technique being active or its Accuracy > Life condition being met, despite the earlier progress report.
findings.action: Do not rely on its damage bonus until a fresh export shows it allocated and Accuracy exceeds Life; verify the live tree in game.

source.note: Original dashboard plan based on the 3.30 Cyclone Shockwave Slayer concept and its published HCSSF campaign testing. The campaign PoB checkpoints were exported against treeVersion 3_29; every named node ID in this plan was checked against the current Community PoB 3_30 tree data. These are planned checkpoints only, not current character allocations.

plan.core: Physical two-handed staff Cyclone with Shockwave for broad clear; add Void Shockwave if it drops. Keep a separate General's Cry plus Sunder or Ground Slam of Earthshaking setup for bosses and tough rares. Start with regular Cyclone; Cyclone of Tumult and The Stampede are optional upgrades, not requirements.
patch330: Slayer Impact: 5% increased Area of Effect per enemy killed recently, up to 50%. This should widen Cyclone coverage as packs die.
Slayer Endless Hunger: 20% increased Attack Speed while Leeching. Cyclone hits frequently and should maintain leech against live packs and bosses.

leveling.focus: Fast physical one-handed weapon; use a vendor physical-damage craft when upgrades stall. Move into the Duelist life and physical-attack route.
Static Strike with Ancestral Call and Ruthless. Continue life and two-handed physical damage; use a staff or mace if Shockwave is the direction, but do not force a weak weapon.
Swap to regular Cyclone only when it feels better and a suitable staff/mace is equipped. Add Shockwave after its level requirement and link are available; keep Static Strike or Sunder as fallback.
Build the life and staff-block foundation. Keep a separate Sunder or General’s Cry setup for single target; weapon upgrades matter more than small damage nodes.

passivePrinciples: Prioritize life and the life mastery before optional damage; keep a defensive point reserve if the next boss is a known danger.

Move from Duelist starting life and physical attack clusters toward two-handed/staff damage and staff block. Keep early damage efficient; refine exact route against the matching 3.30 tree when the character is created.
Pick up staff block investment (including Whirling Barrier / Steelwood Stance where the verified route supports it) and impale scaling after the life foundation.
Avoid early crit commitment. Keep accuracy reliable through weapon and gear upgrades, then follow the crit or non-crit route supported by your drops.
End campaign with capped elemental resistances after Kitava penalties, a strong life pool, bleed removal, and a usable life flask before adding optional damage.
ascendancy: Normal Lab: Brutal Fervour for persistent leech recovery.
Cruel Lab: Endless Hunger for the 3.30 attack-speed-while-leeching bonus and leeching defenses.
Merciless Lab: Impact for the 3.30 kill-based AoE that improves pack clear.
Uber Lab: Bane of Legends for the final damage / mapping payoff; complete only when safe.

ssfGear: Default armour base: Armour/Evasion hybrid. Pure Armour is a good alternative when life/resists/sockets are better. Armour/ES and ES bases are not targets because the build does not scale Energy Shield.
Weapon is the main damage lever: keep a high physical-DPS staff current with character level. Use vendor physical-damage crafting and bench crafts; do not wait for a unique.
Life on every rare armour slot and jewellery; cap fire, cold, and lightning resistance before entering maps.
Armour bases and endurance-charge access support physical mitigation; staff block is an extra layer, not a substitute for life and max-hit defenses.
Aim for a 4-link through campaign, then 5-link/6-link only as drops and crafting permit.

Armour bases: make Armour/Evasion hybrid rares the default target. They fit the Duelist’s Strength/Dexterity spread and give both physical mitigation and evasion; pure Armour is also good when the item has better life/resists or the sockets fit. Do not deliberately target Armour/ES or ES bases—this build has no Energy Shield scaling. Prioritize life, resistances, links, and usable colours over the base label.

passiveRouteSource.method: Named node IDs and names were checked against the Community PoB 3_30 tree, and the route was verified as connected from Duelist start. It uses the published level 68 tree as its 90-point regular-passive core, substitutes Armour/Evasion and Life (35568) for Unwavering Stance (40907), then adds three connected physical-damage nodes to reach the approximate level-70/all-quest 93-point target.
passiveRouteSource.respecPolicy: No planned respec is required in the default Armour/Evasion route. Optional one-point swap: refund node 35568 and allocate Unwavering Stance 40907 if stun immunity is more valuable than evasion. This is a clear defensive trade, not a mandatory upgrade.
